# Problem statement

*Which genes are differentially expressed between patients with complete response and patients with progressive disease following anti-PD-L1 treatment?*

**Suggested tasks:**

• Prepare and explore the gene-expression data, including appropriate filtering and

normalization.

• Perform differential expression analysis between responders/non-responder using

DESeq2, and identify significantly differentially expressed genes

• Visualize the results using e.g. volcano plots and heatmaps of selected genes.

• Investigate the biological functions of differentially expressed genes and discuss their

potential relevance to immunotherapy response.

• Discuss the limitations of the analysis, including potential confounding factors and

why differential expression does not necessarily imply a causal role in treatment

response.

## Load data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(DESeq2)
```

```{r}
data <- readRDS("/home/projects/22123/IMvigor210_plain.rds")
```

```{r}
clinical <- data$clinical  
counts <- data$counts      
tpm <- data$tpm
```

## Clean data

#### Check for overlapping samples

Clinical

```{r}
head(clinical)
```

Counts

```{r}
dim(counts)
```

We don't use TPM for gene expression analysis

```{r}
overlapping_samples <- intersect(colnames(counts), clinical$sample_id)
```

The datasets are complete, all samples overlap.

#### Check if the data is in the right format for DESeq2

DESeq2 needs a wide count matrix: genes in rows, samples in columns.

Counts matrix already has genes in rows and samples in columns.

Clinical data already has sample id as row names, so we just need to convert R/NR to a factor

```{r}
clinical$BOR <- as.factor(clinical$BOR)
```

"NR" "R" confirms "NR" (progression disease) is the reference level, so all fold changes downstream mean “higher in patients who responded” when positive.

```{r}
levels(clinical$BOR)
```

Get a table of which and how many values there are in the BOR column

```{r}
table(clinical$BOR)
```

#### Make sure the sample ids are aligned

DESeq2 does not check that.

```{r}
clinical <- clinical[overlapping_samples, ]
counts <- counts[, overlapping_samples]
```

Check the sample order between the matrix and metadata

```{r}
colnames(counts) == rownames(clinical)
```

## DESeq2

```{r}
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = counts,
  colData = clinical,
  design = ~ BOR
)
```

Compute, for each gene, the total read count summed across all 192 samples, and keeps only genes with at least 10 total reads.

Genes below that are almost certainly too sparsely expressed to reach significance, and including them would waste statistical power (more tests means a harsher multiple-testing correction) without any real chance of a useful result.

```{r}
keep <- rowSums(counts(dds)) >= 10
dds <- dds[keep, ]
```

Removed 8084 elements

```{r}
dds <- DESeq(dds)
```

1.  size-factor normalization (adjusts for differing sequencing depth between samples),
2.   per-gene dispersion (variance) estimation,
3.   and a Wald test per gene for the BOR coefficient.

```{r}
res <- results(dds, alpha=0.05)
```

## DESeq2 results

```{r}
summary(res)
```

23000 genes\
167 up\
278 down

## Volcano plot

```{r}
res_df <- as_data_frame(res) |>
mutate(significant = padj < 0.05)
```

```{r}
res_df_2 <- as_tibble(res, rownames = "gene") |>
drop_na(padj, log2FoldChange) |>
mutate(
group = case_when(
padj < 0.05 & log2FoldChange < 0 ~ "Up in patients with disease progression",
padj < 0.05 & log2FoldChange > 0 ~ "Up in patients who responded",
TRUE ~ "Not significant"
)
)
top_labels <- res_df_2 |>
filter(group != "Not significant") |>
slice_min(padj, n = 10)
ggplot(res_df_2, aes(x = log2FoldChange, y = -log10(padj))) +
geom_point(aes(color = group)) +
geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
scale_color_manual(
name = NULL,
values = c(
"Up in patients with disease progression" = "firebrick",
"Up in patients who responded" = "steelblue",
"Not significant" = "grey80"
)
) +
geom_text(
data = top_labels,
aes(label = gene),
size = 3,
vjust = -0.6,
check_overlap = TRUE
) +
labs(x = "Log2 Fold Change",
y = "-Log10 Adjusted P-value",
title = "Volcano Plot") +
theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position="bottom")
```

#### Results interpretation

445 genes flagged significant ( padj \< 0.05)

3571 genes have NA padj (independent filtering) and are dropped from the plot

log2FoldChange ranges from about -7.3 to +3 across all tested genes

Top up genes (higher in patients who responded) by fold change include MYH15 and WDR87 with high effect and sifnificance.

Top down genes (higher in patients with disease progression ) include ALB, HABP2 and FGB.


## Heat map
```{r}
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-align: center

library(pheatmap)

# Select the 20 most significant differentially expressed genes
top_genes <- as.data.frame(res) |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("gene") |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(padj), padj < 0.05) |>
  dplyr::arrange(padj) |>
  head(20) |>
  dplyr::pull(gene)

# Variance stabilizing transformation
vsd <- vst(dds, blind = FALSE)

# Extract expression values for selected genes
heatmap_data <- assay(vsd)[top_genes, , drop = FALSE]

# Order patients by treatment response
sample_order <- order(colData(dds)$BOR)
heatmap_data <- heatmap_data[, sample_order, drop = FALSE]

# Create response group annotation
annotation_col <- data.frame(
  Response = colData(dds)$BOR[sample_order],
  row.names = colnames(heatmap_data)
)

annotation_colors <- list(
  Response = c(
    "NR" = "#00BFC4",
    "R" = "#F8766D"
  )
)

# Standardize expression for each gene
heatmap_scaled <- t(scale(t(heatmap_data)))

# Limit extreme values for better visualization
heatmap_scaled[heatmap_scaled > 2] <- 2
heatmap_scaled[heatmap_scaled < -2] <- -2

# Create heatmap
pheatmap(
  heatmap_scaled,
  scale = "none",
  color = colorRampPalette(
    c("#2166AC", "white", "#B2182B")
  )(100),
  breaks = seq(-2, 2, length.out = 101),
  annotation_col = annotation_col,
  annotation_colors = annotation_colors,
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  cluster_cols = FALSE,
  gaps_col = sum(annotation_col$Response == "NR"),
  show_colnames = FALSE,
  fontsize_row = 10,
  cellheight = 15,
  border_color = NA,
  main = "Top 20 Differentially Expressed Genes",
  legend = TRUE
)
```

## Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA)
```{r}
library(fgsea)
library(msigdbr)
```

#### Rank genes for the GSEA
```{r}
ranked_genes <- res$stat
names(ranked_genes) <- rownames(res)

# Remove missing values
ranked_genes <- ranked_genes[!is.na(ranked_genes)]

# Sort genes from highest to lowest
ranked_genes <- sort(ranked_genes, decreasing = TRUE)

# Inspect the ranked genes
head(ranked_genes)
```

#### Verify the gene IDs are compatible with the gene sets
```{r}
head(names(ranked_genes))
resultsNames(dds)
```

#### Load biological pathways
```{r}
gene_sets_df <- msigdbr(
  species = "Homo sapiens",
  category = "C5",
  subcategory = "GO:BP"
)

gene_sets <- split(
  gene_sets_df$gene_symbol,
  gene_sets_df$gs_name
)
```

```{r}
head(gene_sets_df)
length(gene_sets)
```

```{r}
set.seed(42)

fgsea_res <- fgsea(
  pathways = gene_sets,
  stats = ranked_genes,
  nPermSimple = 10000
)

fgsea_res <- fgsea_res |>
  dplyr::arrange(padj)
```


#### Visualize the top enriched pathway
```{r}
topPathways <- fgsea_res |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(padj)) |>
  dplyr::slice_min(padj, n = 10)

ggplot(
  topPathways,
  aes(x = reorder(pathway, NES), y = NES, fill = NES > 0)
) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("firebrick", "steelblue"),
    labels = c(
      "Progressive disease",
      "Complete response"
    ),
    name = "Enriched in"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Biological pathway",
    y = "Normalized Enrichment Score (NES)",
    title = "GSEA of anti-PD-L1 treatment response"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

#### Identify the significant pathways
```{r}
significant_pathways <- fgsea_res |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(padj), padj < 0.05) |>
  dplyr::select(pathway, NES, padj, size)

print(significant_pathways, n = 30)
```

```{r}
# Select the most significant pathway
top_pathway <- fgsea_res |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(padj)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(padj) |>
  dplyr::slice(1) |>
  dplyr::pull(pathway)

# Plot enrichment
plotEnrichment(
  gene_sets[[top_pathway]],
  ranked_genes
) +
  labs(title = top_pathway)
```
